test_title: PYST 17: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 14 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 33 minutes and 22 minutes, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 18 minutes. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM(33, 22, 18) = 198 units.

Efficiency of filling Pipe A = 198 ÷ 33 = +6 units/min.

Efficiency of filling Pipe B = 198 ÷ 22 = +9 units/min.

Combined Efficiency (A + B − C) = 198 ÷ 18 = +11 units/min.

Efficiency of emptying Pipe C = (6 + 9) − 11 = 4 units/min.

Time taken by Pipe C to empty = 198 ÷ 4 = 49.5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 49.5 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 33 minutes

⇒ Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 22 minutes

⇒ Time taken by all three pipes (A, B and emptying Pipe C) to fill = 18 minutes

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Work = Efficiency × Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of the emptying pipe C be x.

⇒ Total efficiency when all pipes are open = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of C

⇒ 11 = 6 + 9 − x

⇒ 11 = 15 − x

⇒ x = 4 units/min.

⇒ Time taken by Pipe C to empty the completely filled cistern = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken = 198 ÷ 4

⇒ Time taken = 49.5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 49.5 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Sign Convention

In pipe and cistern problems, the work done by a filling pipe is considered positive (+), whereas the work done by an emptying pipe or leak is taken as negative (−).

Efficiency & Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. For any setup, Total Capacity = Efficiency × Time.

Combined Work Rule

If pipe A can fill a tank in x hours and pipe B can empty it in y hours (where y > x), the net part filled in 1 hour is given by (1/x) − (1/y).
